subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should the browser tool make compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals the default interaction contract, or keep the current capped snapshot behavior with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: Current main already has caps, optional efficient snapshots, and generic context guards, but the remaining change affects model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with existing full snapshot workflows.

options.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
options.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

options.title: Keep current capped behavior
options.body: Retain current AI snapshot caps and opt-in efficient mode, and treat additional browser compaction as future targeted work.

options.title: Fold into broader browser ergonomics work
options.body: Track the action-diff and stale-state pieces under the broader browser automation umbrella while keeping this issue focused on context-budget semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the browser plugin's public interaction contract and compatibility boundary, which history ties most strongly to the snapshot default and bundled-plugin ownership work.
